title: Separate similar pairs
hook: Two almost identical labels need a distinguishing cue.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: that two near-identical items get mixed up unless the note records the one detail that tells them apart

misconception: Two very similar items can be learned from the same description.
objective: Check the specific difference between two arbitrary codes.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: Two almost identical labels need a distinguishing cue. Which notes distinguish these codes? Correct option: Code plus distinguishing field. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.
claims.source: Explicit exercise fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts and pure rules in studyModels.ts. All times, sizes, deadlines and outcomes describe this exercise only; no empirical productivity or learning effect is inferred. claims.text: The last digit distinguishes the two codes in the fixture. The same shared description would not identify which code was intended.
claims.source: Roediger & Karpicke (2006), Test-Enhanced Learning, Psychological Science 17(3),249–255, DOI10.1111/j.1467-9280.2006.01693.x; publisher abstract retrieved 2026-10-13: https://www.psychologicalscience.org/journals/psychological-science/j.1467-9280.2006.01693.x/ .
